web_evidence.title: See Me Preview — Nicholas Sparks
web_evidence.note: The author's 23-page preview sustains third-person narration through the unnamed stalker's prologue and Chapter 1, which is headed 'Colin' and externally narrates Colin's actions, perceptions, and thoughts.

web_evidence.title: Acts of Terror Committed by the Antagonist in Nicholas Sparks's See Me
web_evidence.note: This scholarly analysis uses the novel as its primary text and explicitly states that the story is told in third person.

web_evidence.title: “See Me” by Nicholas Sparks Book Review | CCPL Writers' Block
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly describes the novel as alternating between Colin and Maria by chapter while remaining in third person; these are focal-character changes, not changes of grammatical person.

search_log: Searched: Nicholas Sparks See Me excerpt first chapter publisher; See Me Nicholas Sparks point of view third person narrator; See Me Nicholas Sparks Google Books excerpt Colin Maria; See Me Nicholas Sparks alternating point of view.
Opened and inspected the official 23-page Nicholas Sparks PDF preview, including the third-person prologue and Chapter 1 headed 'Colin.'
Searched targeted combinations for "See Me" with "third person," "alternating third-person," and "point of view" plus Colin and Maria.

Opened a scholarly Journal Albion article that explicitly identifies third-person narration across the novel and a CCPL review describing chapter-level alternation between third-person focal characters.

Hachette and Google Books pages were checked but supplied catalog synopsis rather than diagnostic prose or an explicit POV description; StoryGraph reviews helped locate the prologue and rotating focal-character structure but were not needed as primary evidence.
person_note: The base narration is third person. The clearest quote evidence is the sustained third-person rendering of the woman's reflections in q02295 and the external scene beats around Colin and Evan in q02304; first-person forms elsewhere occur in dialogue or gnomic material. The authorized opening independently sustains third person across both an unnamed stalker prologue and Colin's first chapter, while scholarly whole-book analysis explicitly confirms third person. Reviews describe chapters rotating between Colin and Maria, but both strands remain third person, so this is not ALTERNATING under the person-label definition. No credible first- or second-person base section was found; the only residual limitation is that the authorized prose sample covers the opening rather than the entire novel.
